LESSON: KENYAN INDIGENOUS GAMES (OPTIONAL)

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.2: Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional), part of Strand 12 in Grade 8 CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS.

Key inquiry question: How do indigenous tagging skills enhance physical fitness? 2. Why is tagging considered an indigenous game?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify types of indigenous tagging games played in Kenya,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. perform different indigenous tagging games for skill acquisition,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. perform indigenous tagging games using musical rhythm for coordination,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the role played by indigenous tagging games for enjoyment.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify types of indigenous tagging games played in Kenya,

   Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. perform different indigenous tagging games for skill acquisition,

   Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. perform indigenous tagging games using musical rhythm for coordination,

   Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the role played by indigenous tagging games for enjoyment.

   Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch virtual or live performance of indigenous tagging games and identify the types of games observed,

2. demonstrate skills in different indigenous tagging games while observing safety,

3. practise different indigenous tagging games while observing safety

4. practise different indigenous tagging games with background musical rhythm. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch virtual or live performance of indigenous tagging games and identify the types of games observed,
2. demonstrate skills in different indigenous tagging games while observing safety,
3. practise different indigenous tagging games while observing safety
4. practise different indigenous tagging games with background musical rhythm. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Responsibility: the learner takes on different roles during indigenous tagging games.

• Unity: the learner works with others in indigenous tagging games

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Safety: the learner observes safety rules when playing indigenous tagging games.

• Health and Fitness: the learner improves fitness through indigenous tagging games for a healthy lifestyle.

Link to other learning areas:

Mathematics: the learner keeps counting during indigenous tagging games.
